title: Limits on Taking Part of a Certificate of Deposit
content:
Not every tier of the Certificates of Deposit line lets an owner take part of the principal and leave the rest running. Where a tier does, four figures bound it.

## Limits by tier

| Tier | Part of the principal may be taken early | Smallest single early partial withdrawal, USD | Principal that must remain after one, USD | Most early partial withdrawals in a term | Credited interest may be withdrawn without penalty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6-Month Certificate | no | not applicable | not applicable | 0 | no |
| 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate | no | not applicable | not applicable | 0 | yes |
| 12-Month Certificate | yes | 500.00 | 1000.00 | 2 | yes |
| 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate | yes | 500.00 | 2500.00 | 2 | yes |
| 36-Month Certificate | yes | 500.00 | 1000.00 | 2 | yes |
| 60-Month Certificate | yes | 500.00 | 1000.00 | 2 | yes |

## Points of judgement

The two tiers that permit no early partial withdrawal show "not applicable" for the two amount figures and 0 for the count; there is no smaller figure that would let a part-withdrawal through on them.

The smallest withdrawal and the balance that must remain are separate figures and both bind at once. On an 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate the sum taken must be at least 500.00 USD and at least 2500.00 USD must still stand afterwards; on a 12-Month, 36-Month or 60-Month Certificate the figure that must remain is 1000.00 USD.

Withdrawing interest already credited during the term is not the same act as withdrawing principal, and the last column is about that act alone. It is open on every tier except the 6-Month Certificate, including the two tiers that permit no partial withdrawal of principal.
